page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading. It provides a substantial L3 cache allocation of 260 MB, alongside 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included on this instance type, requiring external Premium Storage attachments for persistent data needs, and it operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Instruction set features for the underlying processor include AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and INT8 matrix calculations, alongside cryptographic accelerations like VAES and SHA_NI. In standard benchmarks, the E8s_v6 delivers strong single-core performance, scoring 1966.0 on Geekbench single-core and showing high efficiency in single-threaded gzip compression at 31.4 GB/sec and text processing at 2585.0 points. Multi-core performance lands squarely in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core result of 7679.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14266.07.

Memory throughput reaches 67.48 GB/sec read and 46.48 GB/sec write for large 256 MB blocks, supporting workloads like in-memory key-value caching where it executes 11.39 million Redis SET operations per second. However, CPU-based execution of larger language models exhibits distinct limits; while small 135M model generation reaches 247.79 tokens per second, medium 7B model generation drops to 8.03 tokens per second, and large 70B models prove impractical due to core counts and lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8s_v6 presents an economical configuration for workloads requiring a generous 8:1 memory-to-core ratio without paying for unused multi-core density. Because local storage is absent, the overall deployment cost is dependent on attached storage tiers. It is particularly well suited for enterprise database hosting, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, business logic processing, and data preparation pipelines.

The instance features a high 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio and a large 260 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It includes no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the E8s_v6 demonstrates strong single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 1966.0 and fast single-threaded gzip compression, while multi-core compute and PassMark results remain in the median range. In-memory performance is validated by 11.39 million Redis SET operations per second. Given its resource profile, the instance provides qualitative cost advantages for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extensive parallel core scaling, such as relational databases, in-memory caches, and general business application servers.
